### 🖼️ Your own screenshot as a map's picture
- The map settings dialog now shows what the lobby will show, and lets you upload a screenshot of your own instead of the editor's automatic render. Replace it or take it away whenever you like - the automatic one comes back.
- The picture you upload is what everyone sees: the lobby's map list, the rotation ballot between matches, and your maps on the web profile.
- Deleting a map takes its screenshot with it.

### 🚧 Maps you can show before they are finished
- A "Coming soon" switch in the map settings lists your map for everyone with a badge on it, while only you can start a game on it. It stays out of the between-match rotation until you release it.

### ⚠️ PvE says what it is
- The main menu and both PvE lobby tabs now say out loud that PvE is early in development, so nobody finds it out over an evening. PvP is the finished half.
- A "Favorite" badge marks the modes and maps we recommend.
- An "About" tile in the main menu opens the site in your browser.

### 🎒 The bag key is on the HUD
- A backpack card next to the ammo counter says which key opens your inventory (or the buy menu in PvP). It shows the key you actually have bound, and is hidden in the modes with no loadout panel.

### ⎋ Esc keeps you in fullscreen
- In the browser, pausing and resuming with Esc no longer drops you out of fullscreen behind your own back. Esc closes the pause menu again, the way it always did in the desktop app.
- Leaving fullscreen is now press-and-hold Esc, or F11, or the window-mode switch in the settings.

### 💥 A grenade no longer falls through a tilted platform
- Lob one onto a sloped platform and it lands on it. It used to bounce off the underside and be set down on the roof, or drop through the floor at the rim.

### 🛠️ Map editor
- The toolbar fits a laptop again: snapping, the overlays, the ground brushes and the document actions moved into drop-down menus that say what is switched on, and the bar drops to a second row rather than squeezing the labels off its buttons.
- The bottom shortcut strip grows when it wraps instead of hiding its last hint under the edge of the window.
